description: Coinbase rose ~16.5% on 2026-02-13, the session after its Q4'25 shareholder letter was furnished on an Item 2.02 8-K. The inverse of the NVDA trap: the headline quarter got WORSE sequentially - total revenue $1.8B down 5% Q/Q, transaction revenue down 6% Q/Q, opex up 9% Q/Q - yet the stock rallied hard. A naive reading of the numbers alone points the wrong direction.

trigger.verified_fact: Close-to-close gain of ~16.5% on 2026-02-13, from $141.09 to $164.32.
trigger.note: Real daily closes from Yahoo Finance. The stock had fallen for four straight sessions into the print.

filing.item: 2.02 Results of Operations and Financial Condition

ground_truth.one_line: The Q4'25 shareholder letter is unambiguously the catalyst, but the filing-grounded story is full-year strength and capital returns, not the sequentially weaker quarter.
key_facts_from_filing: Q4 total revenue was $1.8 billion, down 5% Q/Q.
Q4 transaction revenue was $983 million, down 6% Q/Q; subscription and services revenue was $727 million, down 3% Q/Q.
Q4 net income was $178 million and Adjusted EBITDA was $566 million.
Coinbase ended 2025 with $11.3 billion in cash and cash equivalents and repurchased $1.7 billion of Class A common stock; fully diluted weighted average share count fell 8% Q/Q to 268 million.
ground_truth.key_facts_note: All stated in the Q4'25 shareholder letter (EX-99.1).
market_context: The stock had already fallen four consecutive sessions into the print, so positioning going in was defensive.
The scale of the rally implies results landed better than the market was positioned for.
ground_truth.market_context_note: Requires knowledge of expectations and positioning, which the filing does not contain. Excluded from correctness.
ground_truth.expected_citation: Exhibit 99.1 shareholder letter (ex99_1_shareholder_letter), and optionally the 8-K body.
ground_truth.naive_failure_mode: A system that reads only the sequential headline figures sees revenue down, transaction revenue down, and opex up, and concludes the stock should have fallen - or declares no catalyst. The correct behavior is to identify the earnings release as the catalyst, ground the positive case in what the filing actually supports (full-year revenue growth, $11.3B cash, $1.7B buyback, share count down 8%), and be honest that the filing alone does not fully account for a 16.5% move.

provenance.sources: Figures read directly from the Q4'25 shareholder letter in EDGAR accession 0001679788-26-000011; daily closes from Yahoo Finance.
